evidence: src/presentation/web/TicketController.ts: TicketController.buy contains `if (body.seats < 1 || body.seats > 8) { throw new TicketRejected('Between 1 and 8 seats per purchase'); }`, which is a purchase-limit business rule in a presentation file
The rule throws TicketRejected from src/business/core/TicketingError.ts, a domain rejection, which shows this is a domain policy and not input formatting
The rest of the file is presentation work: BuyBody/ScanBody DTOs, delegation to BoxOffice.purchase/admit/listing and GateLog.scanned, and response formatting with euros()
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Most of TicketController is normal presentation work. It defines the request body shapes, hands off to BoxOffice and GateLog, and formats money with euros() for the response. The exception is TicketController.buy, which enforces 'Between 1 and 8 seats per purchase' and throws the domain error TicketRejected. Checking that seats is at least 1 could pass as input validation. The upper limit of 8 seats per purchase is a business policy, though, and it belongs in the domain layer (business), for example in BoxOffice.purchase. Because the rule lives in the controller, any other entry point that calls BoxOffice.purchase skips the limit.
